references.text: These verses give detailed laws about a woman's impurity during menstruation and the consequences for anyone who has sexual relations with her during this period. The terms 'דָּוָה' (menstruating) and 'מְקוֹר דָּמֶיהָ' (her source of blood) are used in both texts.
This verse directly forbids sexual intercourse with a woman during her menstruation. Leviticus 20:18 gives the penalty for violating this prohibition.
The same penalty expression 'וְנִכְרְתוּ' (they shall be cut off) is used for sexual offenses, showing a connection in the penal code.
Ezekiel uses menstrual impurity as a metaphor for Jerusalem's sin and uncleanness, referring to this practice as detestable.
Ezekiel lists sexual intercourse with a menstruating woman as one of the sins committed in Jerusalem, directly linked to the prohibition in Leviticus.
